anthology

an-THOL-uh-jee — the root means 'flower'; an anthology is literally a gathering of the best flowers, or writings. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Anthology is a published collection of writings by different authors.

The teacher assigned a poetry anthology featuring works from a dozen different award-winning poets.

Example

An editor spends a year reading thousands of short stories submitted by writers all over the world, then selects the twenty best to be printed together as a single anthology under one title.

That single book gathering together the best work of many different writers is what makes it an anthology. Unlike a 'novel,' which is one continuous story by one author, an anthology brings together separate works from separate voices.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

collection: A collection is any group of things gathered together -- seashells on a shelf, stamps in a binder -- with no editor and no publication required. An anthology is a published, deliberately edited gathering of writings by different authors.

miscellany: A miscellany is a mixed bag of assorted pieces with no unifying thread -- whatever happened to be at hand. An anthology is the opposite in spirit: its editor gathers different authors' writings around one shared theme or purpose.

treasury: A treasury gathers especially prized or beloved pieces -- the emphasis falls on showcasing acknowledged favorites. An anthology needs no famous contents at all; it simply brings different authors' works together around a theme, celebrated or not.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

single work: one standalone piece by one author

solo piece: a work created by a single individual alone

Where it sits · how broad the gathered contents can be

omnibus → anthology → compilation

omnibus vs. anthology: An omnibus is narrower than an anthology -- it reprints in one volume works that already appeared separately, most often a single author's, while an anthology can range across many different authors' writings, brand-new or old.

compilation vs. anthology: Compilation is a broader word than anthology -- a compilation can gather almost anything (songs, videos, statistics), while anthology specifically refers to a curated collection of literary writing.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — antho-: flower (Greek anthos; the -o- is the Greek linking vowel)

root — -logy: collection, gathering (from Greek legein, 'to gather, choose'; later also 'study of')

Put it together: Greek anthos meant 'flower,' and -logy meant 'a gathering.' An anthology, at its root, is literally 'a gathering of flowers' -- an old poetic image for a collection of the finest, most carefully chosen writings.

Use the root in a new word: chrysanthemum: Golden chrysanthemums bloomed along the garden path every autumn.
